chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both) said:
"The divorced woman performs Hajj during her waiting period."
The meaning is if her Hajj is the Hajj of Islam (obligatory); if her Hajj is voluntary, it is not permissible for her to leave during the waiting period, according to what we have previously stated.
This is indicated by what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: Can a divorced woman perform Hajj during her waiting period (Iddah)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of the penalties for unintentional violations during Hajj, clarifying that a divorced woman is permitted to perform her obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam) during her 'iddah, whereas voluntary Hajj is restricted. This distinction highlights the juristic view that the primary religious duty takes precedence over the general prohibition on a woman leaving her residence without a mahram or permission during the waiting period.
